# RKI data on reported cases

RKI provides the daily number of new confirmed COVID-19 cases in Germany, available at the county level (IdLandkreis, starts with "11" for Berlin, "12" for Brandenburg), broken down by age group and gender. The data can be differentiated into "Meldedatum", which is the date of reporting, and "Refdatum", which is either the assumed date of the actual onset, or if unknown, the date of reporting.

The data is available in CSV format and can be downloaded from <https://github.com/robert-koch-institut/SARS-CoV-2-Infektionen_in_Deutschland_Archiv>

For the ODE fit, it seems that we used "Refdatum", which is the date of the actual onset or reporting date, and not "Meldedatum", which is the date of reporting. However, for the ABM, I think we used "Meldedatum" - this might make sense if the ABM enables to simulate the reporting process, while the ODE's I-compartment simulates the actual disease progression.

```{r}
# Helper function to process and aggregate RKI data
process_rki_data <- function(df, date_col, region_prefix = "11") {
  df %>%
    filter(str_starts(as.character(IdLandkreis), region_prefix)) %>%
    group_by(date = as_date(.data[[date_col]])) %>%
    summarise(daily_new = sum(AnzahlFall, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    complete(date = seq(min(date), max(date), by = "1 day"), fill = list(daily_new = 0)) %>%
    arrange(date)
}
```

Load RKI data from Github

```{r}
# Load data from the RKI GitHub repository
rki_repo_url <- "https://github.com/robert-koch-institut/SARS-CoV-2-Infektionen_in_Deutschland_Archiv/raw/refs/heads/main/Archiv/2021-05-31_Deutschland_SarsCov2_Infektionen.csv.xz"

# Download to a temp file
tmpfile <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv.xz")
download.file(rki_repo_url, tmpfile, mode = "wb")

# Read from compressed file directly
raw_data <- read_csv(tmpfile)
```

calculate incidence for three study areas

Note: when 'align = "right"' rollmean centers the mean around the right date of the range (for 7 observations between Mon & Sun, the value would be set to Sunday)

```{r}
# Load data and process both Refdatum 

date_type <- "Refdatum"
rki_berlin <- process_rki_data(raw_data, date_type) %>% 
  mutate(incidence = rollsum(daily_new, 7, fill = NA,align = "right") / POPULATION_BERLIN * 1e5)

rki_brand <- process_rki_data(raw_data, date_type, region_prefix = "12") %>%
  mutate(incidence = rollsum(daily_new, 7, fill = NA,align = "right") /  POPULATION_BRANDENBURG * 1e5)

rki_combined<- rbind(rki_brand, rki_berlin) %>% group_by(date) %>% 
  summarise(daily_new = sum(daily_new))%>%
  mutate(incidence = rollsum(daily_new, 7, fill = NA,align = "right") / (POPULATION_BRANDENBURG + POPULATION_BERLIN) * 1e5)


```

## Combined: Berlin + Brandenburg

```{r}


# the "-br" in the directory means that we filter the outputs to only include landkreise in brandenburg. This is a bit different to what is shown on covid-sim, where I believe the incidence of the entire study area (berlin, brand, and other bundesländer) is shown. 
combined_directory <- paste0(analysis_20260203, "1-both-br/")


combined_districts <- c("Berlin", brand_districts)


# these are the settings we've chosen for our paper!
combined_info <- read_delim(paste0(combined_directory, "_info.txt"), delim = ";") %>% 
    filter(thetaFactor %in% c(0.75), maxOutdoorFraction == 1.0, importMultSpring %in% c(0.25),importToBerlin == FALSE)

# %>% 
  # filter(pHouseholds == 0.35, importMult == 2)

# combined_info %>% view()

combined_raw <- read_combine_episim_output_zipped(combined_directory, combined_info,"infections.txt.csv", c("date","nShowingSymptomsCumulative","nSusceptible","district")) 



combined_params <- get_run_parameters(combined_directory)

combined_filtered_berlin <- combined_raw  %>% filter(district == "Berlin")

combined_filtered_brand <- combined_raw %>% 
  filter(district %in% brand_districts) %>% 
  group_by(across(all_of(c("date",combined_params)))) %>%
  summarise(nShowingSymptomsCumulative = sum(nShowingSymptomsCumulative), nSusceptible = sum(nSusceptible)) %>% 
  mutate(district = "Brandenburg")

combined_filtered_combined <- combined_raw %>% 
  filter(district %in% combined_districts) %>% 
  group_by(across(all_of(c("date",combined_params)))) %>%
  summarise(nShowingSymptomsCumulative = sum(nShowingSymptomsCumulative), nSusceptible = sum(nSusceptible)) %>% 
  mutate(district = "Combined")

combined_filtered <- rbind(combined_filtered_berlin, combined_filtered_brand, combined_filtered_combined)


combined_incidence <- convert_infections_into_incidence(combined_directory,combined_filtered,FALSE)

combined_incidence_filtered <- combined_incidence %>% 
  select(date, incidence, district) %>% 
  mutate(scenario = "Model") %>% 
  rbind(rki_combined %>% select(date, incidence = incidence) %>% mutate(scenario = "Data (RKI)",district = "Combined")) %>% 
  rbind(rki_berlin %>% select(date, incidence = incidence) %>% mutate(scenario = "Data (RKI)",district = "Berlin")) %>% 
  rbind(rki_brand %>% select(date, incidence = incidence) %>% mutate(scenario = "Data (RKI)",district = "Brandenburg")) %>% 
  filter(date >= plot_start_date, date <= plot_end_date) %>% 
  group_by(scenario) %>% 
  mutate(incidence_smooth = rollmean(incidence, k = 7, fill = NA, align = "center")) %>%
  filter(lubridate::wday(date, label = TRUE)=="Thu") %>%
  ungroup()

combined_plot_combined <- ggplot(data = combined_incidence_filtered %>% filter(district == "Combined"), aes(date,incidence_smooth, col = scenario, fill = scenario), group = scenario) +
  geom_line(data = subset(combined_incidence_filtered, scenario == "Model"), size = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 1.75, show.legend = FALSE) +  
  labs(title ="Incidence in Berlin + Brandenburg", subtitle = "Berlin + Brandenburg modelled as ABM") +
  common_style +
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = c(2, 17))))

combined_plot_combined

combined_plot_berlin <- ggplot(data = combined_incidence_filtered %>% filter(district == "Berlin"), aes(date,incidence_smooth, col = scenario, fill = scenario), group = scenario) +
  geom_line(data = subset(combined_incidence_filtered, scenario == "Model"), size = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 1.75) +  
  labs(title ="Incidence in Berlin", subtitle = "Berlin + Brandenburg modelled as ABM") +
  common_style + guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = c(2, 17))))

combined_plot_berlin

combined_plot_brand <- ggplot(data = combined_incidence_filtered %>% filter(district == "Brandenburg"), aes(date,incidence_smooth, col = scenario, fill = scenario), group = scenario) +
  geom_line(data = subset(combined_incidence_filtered, scenario == "Model"), size = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 1.75) +  
  labs(title ="Incidence in Brandenburg", subtitle = "Berlin + Brandenburg modelled as ABM") +
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = c(2, 17)))) +
  common_style 

combined_plot_brand


# plot all three
combined_plot <- combined_plot_combined / (combined_plot_brand | combined_plot_berlin)  + plot_annotation(tag_levels = 'A')
# combined_plot

ggsave(paste0(image_output_path,"results_combined.pdf"), plot = combined_plot, width = 12, height = 8)
```

# Brandenburg Policies

Baseline versus a subset of policies, averaging all five seeds with the same Brandenburg district coverage for every run, using the regular infections output. The plot shows symptom-onset incidence; total infections in the table include asymptomatic infections. Reductions are relative to baseline over the common reporting period, not just the plotted date range.

```{r brandenburg-policies}
# Defined here because this section precedes the correlation analysis.
correlation_directory <- paste0(analysis_20261103, "3-brand-comm/")
policy_expected_seeds <- 5L
policy_start <- "2020-09-01"
policy_scope <- "all"
policy_shares <- seq(0.0,1.0,0.1)
# Match percentages as integers to avoid floating-point equality dropping shares.
# This batch has no OFF runs; COMMUTERS at 0% is the no-intervention baseline.
policy_info <- read_delim(paste0(correlation_directory, "_info.txt"), delim = ";",
                         col_types = cols(seed = col_character())) %>%
  mutate(policy_share_pct = as.integer(round(100 * commuterQuarantineShare))) %>%
  filter(ode == 1, commuterQuarantineDate == policy_start,
         commuterQuarantineScope == policy_scope,
         commuterQuarantineMode %in% c("COMMUTERS", "GENERAL"),
         policy_share_pct %in% as.integer(round(100 * policy_shares)),
         commuterQuarantineMode != "GENERAL" | policy_share_pct > 0) %>%
  mutate(scenario = if_else(policy_share_pct == 0, "Baseline",
    paste(commuterQuarantineMode, percent(policy_share_pct / 100, accuracy = 1))),
    archive = paste0(correlation_directory, "summaries/", RunId, ".zip")) %>%
  arrange(policy_share_pct != 0, commuterQuarantineMode, policy_share_pct)
policy_scenarios <- unique(policy_info$scenario)
policy_seeds <- sort(unique(policy_info$seed))
stopifnot(length(policy_seeds) == policy_expected_seeds,
          sum(policy_info$scenario == "Baseline") == policy_expected_seeds,
          nrow(policy_info) == length(policy_scenarios) * policy_expected_seeds,
          !anyDuplicated(policy_info[c("scenario", "seed")]),
          all(file.exists(policy_info$archive)))

policy_daily <- map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(policy_info)), function(i) {
  run <- policy_info[i, ]
  member <- paste0(run$RunId, ".infections.txt.csv")
  stopifnot(member %in% unzip(run$archive, list = TRUE)$Name)
  raw <- read_tsv(unz(run$archive, member),
    col_select = c(date, district, nSusceptible, nInfectedCumulative, nShowingSymptomsCumulative),
    col_types = cols(date = col_date(), district = col_character(),
      nSusceptible = col_double(), nInfectedCumulative = col_double(),
      nShowingSymptomsCumulative = col_double())) %>%
    filter(district %in% brand_districts)
  stopifnot(nrow(raw) > 0, !anyDuplicated(raw[c("date", "district")]),
            setequal(unique(raw$district), brand_districts))
  coverage <- raw %>% count(date)
  stopifnot(all(coverage$n == n_distinct(raw$district)))
  daily <- raw %>% group_by(date) %>%
    summarise(across(c(nSusceptible, nInfectedCumulative, nShowingSymptomsCumulative), sum),
              .groups = "drop") %>% arrange(date)
  stopifnot(all(diff(as.integer(daily$date)) == 1L), first(daily$nSusceptible) > 0)
  daily %>% mutate(
    population = first(nSusceptible),
    infections = nInfectedCumulative - lag(nInfectedCumulative, default = 0),
    symptom_onsets = nShowingSymptomsCumulative - lag(nShowingSymptomsCumulative, default = 0),
    incidence = (nShowingSymptomsCumulative - lag(nShowingSymptomsCumulative, 7, default = 0)) /
      population * 100000,
    RunId = run$RunId, seed = run$seed, scenario = run$scenario,
    districts = n_distinct(raw$district))
})
# Compare identical dates and geographic coverage; never silently compare truncated runs.
policy_coverage <- policy_daily %>% group_by(scenario, seed) %>%
  summarise(start = min(date), end = max(date), days = n(),
            population = first(population), districts = first(districts), .groups = "drop")
stopifnot(n_distinct(policy_coverage$start) == 1, n_distinct(policy_coverage$end) == 1,
          n_distinct(policy_coverage$days) == 1, all(policy_coverage$population > 0),
          n_distinct(policy_coverage$districts) == 1)

# Evaluation window for all policy statistics (peaks, totals, reductions, gains).
# Spring policy (start before the wave boundary): policy start until the end of the first wave.
# Fall policy: policy start until the end of the simulation.
policy_wave_boundary <- ymd("2020-06-01")
policy_window <- c(ymd(policy_start),
                   if (ymd(policy_start) < policy_wave_boundary) policy_wave_boundary
                   else max(policy_daily$date))
stopifnot(policy_window[1] < policy_window[2])
policy_window_label <- paste(format(policy_window, "%d.%m.%Y"), collapse = "–")
in_policy_window <- function(df) filter(df, date >= policy_window[1], date <= policy_window[2])
# Spring and fall runs write separate output files
policy_output_prefix <- paste0(image_output_path, "results_brand_policies_start-", policy_start)

# Retain per-seed statistics for checking variability separately from the mean curve.
policy_stats_by_seed <- policy_daily %>% in_policy_window() %>% group_by(scenario, seed, RunId) %>%
  summarise(total_infections = sum(infections), max_incidence = max(incidence),
            peak_date = date[which.max(incidence)], .groups = "drop")
policy_daily_mean <- policy_daily %>% group_by(scenario, date) %>%
  summarise(across(c(infections, symptom_onsets, incidence), mean),
            n_seeds = n_distinct(seed), .groups = "drop")
stopifnot(all(policy_daily_mean$n_seeds == policy_expected_seeds))
# Total infections are the mean totals; maximum incidence is the peak of the mean curve.
policy_stats <- policy_daily_mean %>% in_policy_window() %>% group_by(scenario) %>%
  summarise(n_seeds = first(n_seeds), total_infections = sum(infections),
            total_symptom_onsets = sum(symptom_onsets),
            max_incidence = max(incidence), peak_date = date[which.max(incidence)],
            period_start = min(date), period_end = max(date), .groups = "drop")
policy_baseline <- policy_stats %>% filter(scenario == "Baseline")
policy_stats <- policy_stats %>% mutate(
  infections_averted = policy_baseline$total_infections - total_infections,
  infections_reduction_pct = 100 * infections_averted / policy_baseline$total_infections,
  peak_reduction_pct = 100 * (policy_baseline$max_incidence - max_incidence) /
    policy_baseline$max_incidence,
  scenario = factor(scenario, levels = policy_scenarios)) %>% arrange(scenario)

# Plot settings: percentages must be available in policy_shares above; 0 means OFF.
policy_plot_percentages <- seq(20,100,20)
# Named colours can be edited independently; unused percentages keep their colours.
policy_colour_options <- c(
  "OFF" = "#333333", "10%" = "#56B4E9", "20%" = "#009E73",
  "30%" = "#E69F00", "40%" = "#CC79A7", "50%" = "#0072B2",
  "60%" = "#8C564B", "70%" = "#9467BD", "80%" = "#228833",
  "90%" = "#AA3377", "100%" = "#D55E00")
policy_plot_percentages <- sort(unique(policy_plot_percentages))
stopifnot(length(policy_plot_percentages) > 0,
          all(policy_plot_percentages %in% as.integer(round(100 * policy_shares))))
policy_share_labels <- if_else(policy_plot_percentages == 0, "OFF",
                               paste0(policy_plot_percentages, "%"))
stopifnot(all(policy_share_labels %in% names(policy_colour_options)))
policy_plot_scenarios <- c(
  if (0 %in% policy_plot_percentages) "Baseline",
  unlist(lapply(policy_plot_percentages[policy_plot_percentages > 0], function(pct) {
    paste(c("COMMUTERS", "GENERAL"), paste0(pct, "%"))
  })))
stopifnot(all(policy_plot_scenarios %in% policy_scenarios))

# Keep the same centered smoothing and Thursday points as the Brandenburg plot.
policy_plot_data <- policy_daily_mean %>%
  filter(scenario %in% policy_plot_scenarios) %>%
  group_by(scenario) %>% arrange(date, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(incidence_smooth = zoo::rollmean(incidence, 7, fill = NA, align = "center")) %>%
  ungroup() %>% filter(date >= plot_start_date, date <= plot_end_date,
                     lubridate::wday(date, week_start = 1) == 4) %>%
  mutate(share = factor(if_else(scenario == "Baseline", "OFF",
                                str_extract(scenario, "[0-9]+%$")),
                        levels = policy_share_labels),
         policy_type = factor(case_when(
           scenario == "Baseline" ~ "OFF",
           str_starts(scenario, "COMMUTERS") ~ "Commuter",
           TRUE ~ "General"),
           levels = c(if (0 %in% policy_plot_percentages) "OFF",
                      if (any(policy_plot_percentages > 0)) c("Commuter", "General"))))
policy_colours <- policy_colour_options[policy_share_labels]
policy_line_types <- c("OFF" = "solid", "Commuter" = "solid", "General" = "dashed")

policy_base_plot <- ggplot(policy_plot_data,
    aes(date, incidence_smooth, colour = share,
        linetype = policy_type, group = scenario)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1, na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = policy_colours, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = policy_line_types, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 month", date_labels = "%b\n'%y") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  labs(x = "Date", y = "COVID-19 incidence\nper 100,000",
       colour = "Policy share", linetype = "Policy")


ggplot(policy_plot_data |> filter(policy_type == "Commuter"), aes(date, incidence_smooth, colour = share,
                          linetype = policy_type, group = scenario)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1, na.rm = TRUE) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = policy_colours, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = policy_line_types, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 month", date_labels = "%b\n'%y") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
    labs(title = "Commuter policies", x = "Date", y = "COVID-19 incidence\nper 100,000",
         colour = "Policy share", linetype = "Policy") 
    # scale_y_continuous(labels = label_number(),limits = c(0, NA))



# Zero incidence becomes a gap only in the logarithmic panel.
policy_log_data <- policy_plot_data %>%
  mutate(incidence_smooth = if_else(incidence_smooth > 0, incidence_smooth, NA_real_))
policy_full_plot <- policy_base_plot %+% policy_log_data +
  scale_y_log10(labels = label_number(), breaks = c(0.1, 1, 10, 100, 1000)) +
  labs(title = "Full period (log scale)")

policy_first_wave_plot <- policy_base_plot %+%
  filter(policy_plot_data, date <= policy_wave_boundary) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_number(), limits = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(title = "First wave (linear scale)")

policy_second_wave_plot <- policy_base_plot %+%
  filter(policy_plot_data, date > policy_wave_boundary) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_number(), limits = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(title = "Second wave (linear scale)")

policy_second_wave_plot

brand_policy_plot <- (policy_full_plot / (policy_first_wave_plot | policy_second_wave_plot)) +
  patchwork::plot_layout(heights = c(2, 1), guides = "collect") +
  patchwork::plot_annotation(
    title = "Brandenburg: baseline and policy cases",
    subtitle = paste("Mean of", policy_expected_seeds, "seeds | Start:", policy_start,
                     "| Scope:", policy_scope, "| OFF = 0% commuter policy")) &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
brand_policy_plot
```

```{r brandenburg-policies-summary}
knitr::kable(policy_stats, digits = 2, caption =
  "Five-seed means over the full reporting period. Reductions compare mean totals; peak incidence is the unsmoothed peak of the mean curve.")
ggsave(paste0(image_output_path, "results_brand_policies.pdf"), brand_policy_plot, width = 12, height = 10)
write_csv(policy_stats, paste0(image_output_path, "results_brand_policies_stats.csv"))
```

# Brandenburg Policies: decomposition of the policy effect

Each bar is 100% of the OFF value (COMMUTERS 0%). GENERAL x% quarantines the same number of agents as COMMUTERS x%, picked at random, so it is the matched control for the commuter policy. The commuter bar is split into what random quarantine of that many agents achieves (blue) and what targeting commuters adds on top (orange). If targeting does worse than random, the gap is shown in pink instead. Labels give the net reduction; error bars give the range across the paired seeds (per-seed reduction against the same seed's OFF run).

```{r brandenburg-policies-stacked}
# Settings ------------------------------------------------------------------
# One of "total_infections", "total_symptom_onsets", "max_incidence"
policy_metric <- "total_infections"
# FALSE hides the grey "Remaining" part and zooms in on the averted share
policy_show_remaining <- TRUE

policy_metric_label <- c(total_infections = "infections",
                         total_symptom_onsets = "symptom onsets",
                         max_incidence = "peak incidence")[[policy_metric]]

# Averted share per mode and quarantine share (mean over seeds) -------------
policy_effects <- policy_stats %>%
  filter(scenario != "Baseline") %>%
  transmute(mode = str_extract(as.character(scenario), "^[A-Z]+"),
            share_pct = as.integer(str_extract(as.character(scenario), "[0-9]+(?=%$)")),
            averted_pct = 100 * (policy_baseline[[policy_metric]] - .data[[policy_metric]]) /
              policy_baseline[[policy_metric]]) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = mode, values_from = averted_pct) %>%
  arrange(share_pct)
stopifnot(all(c("COMMUTERS", "GENERAL") %in% names(policy_effects)),
          !anyNA(policy_effects$COMMUTERS), !anyNA(policy_effects$GENERAL))
if (any(policy_effects$COMMUTERS < 0 | policy_effects$GENERAL < 0))
  warning("Some policies increase ", policy_metric_label,
          "relative to no NPI (likely seed noise); those segments are drawn below zero.")

# Paired per-seed range (only for metrics available per seed) ---------------
# Note: per-seed max_incidence is each seed's own peak, whereas the bars use the
# peak of the mean curve, so the error bars are only indicative for that metric.
policy_seed_range <- NULL
if (policy_metric %in% names(policy_stats_by_seed)) {
  seed_baseline <- policy_stats_by_seed %>% filter(scenario == "Baseline") %>%
    select(seed, baseline_value = all_of(policy_metric))
  policy_seed_range <- policy_stats_by_seed %>%
    filter(scenario != "Baseline") %>%
    inner_join(seed_baseline, by = "seed") %>%
    mutate(mode = str_extract(scenario, "^[A-Z]+"),
           share_pct = as.integer(str_extract(scenario, "[0-9]+(?=%$)")),
           averted_pct = 100 * (baseline_value - .data[[policy_metric]]) / baseline_value) %>%
    group_by(mode, share_pct) %>%
    summarise(lo = min(averted_pct), hi = max(averted_pct), n = n(), .groups = "drop")
  stopifnot(all(policy_seed_range$n == policy_expected_seeds))
}

# Stack components (each bar sums to 100%) ----------------------------------
lbl_random    <- "Averted by random quarantine of the same # of agents"
lbl_targeting <- "Additionally averted by targeting inter-regional travelers"
lbl_shortfall <- "Would have been averted by random quarantine instead"
lbl_remaining <- paste("Remaining", policy_metric_label)

policy_component_colours <- setNames(
  c("#E0E0E0", "#CC79A7", "#D55E00", "#0072B2"),
  c(lbl_remaining, lbl_shortfall, lbl_targeting, lbl_random))

# First factor level is drawn on top of the stack
stack_levels <- c(lbl_remaining, lbl_shortfall, lbl_targeting, lbl_random)

general_segments <- policy_effects %>%
  transmute(share_pct,
            !!lbl_random := GENERAL,
            !!lbl_remaining := 100 - GENERAL) %>%
  pivot_longer(-share_pct, names_to = "component", values_to = "pct")

commuter_segments <- policy_effects %>%
  transmute(share_pct,
            !!lbl_random := pmin(COMMUTERS, GENERAL),
            !!lbl_targeting := pmax(COMMUTERS - GENERAL, 0),
            !!lbl_shortfall := pmax(GENERAL - COMMUTERS, 0),
            !!lbl_remaining := 100 - pmax(COMMUTERS, GENERAL)) %>%
  pivot_longer(-share_pct, names_to = "component", values_to = "pct")

prepare_segments <- function(segments) {
  segments %>%
    filter(policy_show_remaining | component != lbl_remaining) %>%
    mutate(component = factor(component, levels = stack_levels))
}
general_segments <- prepare_segments(general_segments)
commuter_segments <- prepare_segments(commuter_segments)

# Common y-range so both panels are directly comparable
range_values <- c(0, policy_effects$COMMUTERS, policy_effects$GENERAL,
                  if (!is.null(policy_seed_range)) c(policy_seed_range$lo, policy_seed_range$hi))
policy_y_limits <- c(min(range_values),
                     if (policy_show_remaining) 100 else max(range_values) * 1.1)

# Plot ----------------------------------------------------------------------
plot_policy_stack <- function(mode_name, segments, title) {
  net <- policy_effects %>% transmute(share_pct, averted = .data[[mode_name]])
  if (!is.null(policy_seed_range)) {
    net <- net %>% left_join(filter(policy_seed_range, mode == mode_name), by = "share_pct") %>%
      mutate(label_y = pmax(averted, hi))
  } else {
    net <- net %>% mutate(label_y = averted)
  }

  p <- ggplot(segments, aes(factor(share_pct), pct, fill = component)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.75, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3)
  if (!is.null(policy_seed_range)) {
    p <- p + geom_errorbar(data = net, aes(factor(share_pct), ymin = lo, ymax = hi),
                           inherit.aes = FALSE, width = 0.25, linewidth = 0.4)
  }
  p +
    geom_text(data = net, aes(factor(share_pct), label_y, label = sprintf("%.0f%%", averted)),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, vjust = -0.5, size = 3.5) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = policy_component_colours, drop = FALSE,
                      breaks = rev(stack_levels[stack_levels %in% unique(c(
                        as.character(general_segments$component),
                        as.character(commuter_segments$component)))])) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = label_percent(scale = 1),
                       expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.06))) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = policy_y_limits) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
    theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) +
    labs(title = title, x = "Share of agents quarantined",
         y = paste("Share of unrestricted", policy_metric_label), fill = NULL)
}

policy_stack_general <- plot_policy_stack("GENERAL", general_segments,
                                          "General population")
policy_stack_commuter <- plot_policy_stack("COMMUTERS", commuter_segments,
                                           "Inter-regional travelers")

brand_policy_stack_plot <- (policy_stack_commuter | policy_stack_general) +
  patchwork::plot_layout(guides = "collect") +
  patchwork::plot_annotation(
    subtitle = paste0("Policy start: ", format(ymd(policy_start), "%d.%m.%Y"),
                      " | Evaluated: ", policy_window_label)) &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical")
brand_policy_stack_plot

policy_stack_commuter <- plot_policy_stack("COMMUTERS", commuter_segments,
                                           "Inter-regional travelers") +
  patchwork::plot_annotation(
    subtitle = paste0("Policy start: ", format(ymd(policy_start), "%d.%m.%Y"),
                      " | Evaluated: ", policy_window_label)) &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical")



ggsave(paste0(policy_output_prefix, "_stacked_", policy_metric, ".pdf"),
       brand_policy_stack_plot, width = 12, height = 6.5)
ggsave(paste0(policy_output_prefix, "_stacked_", policy_metric, ".png"),
       brand_policy_stack_plot, width = 12, height = 6.5)

ggsave(paste0(policy_output_prefix, "_stacked_irt_", policy_metric, ".pdf"),
       policy_stack_commuter, width = 6, height = 6.5)
ggsave(paste0(policy_output_prefix, "_stacked_irt_", policy_metric, ".png"),
       policy_stack_commuter, width = 6, height = 6.5)

write_csv(policy_effects,
          paste0(policy_output_prefix, "_decomposition_", policy_metric, ".csv"))
```

# Brandenburg Policies: peak incidence vs. quarantine share

Peak 7-day symptom-onset incidence relative to OFF (COMMUTERS 0%), as a function of the share of agents quarantined. Peaks are taken from `policy_peak_from` onwards, so that the first wave (which is identical in all scenarios) cannot mask the policy effect. Lines: peak of the 5-seed mean curve relative to the OFF mean curve. Ribbons / small points: per-seed peaks relative to the OFF run with the same seed. Bottom panel: how many percentage points more the peak is reduced by targeting commuters than by quarantining the same number of random agents.

```{r brandenburg-policies-peak-vs-share}
# Settings ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Only count peaks from this date on. Use plot_start_date to include the first wave.
policy_peak_from <- ymd(policy_start)

policy_mode_colours <- c("Commuters" = "#D55E00", "General population" = "#0072B2")
policy_mode_linetypes <- c("Commuters" = "solid", "General population" = "dashed")

# Helpers -------------------------------------------------------------------
parse_policy <- function(df) {
  df %>% mutate(
    mode = case_when(scenario == "Baseline" ~ "OFF",
                     str_starts(scenario, "COMMUTERS") ~ "Commuters",
                     str_starts(scenario, "GENERAL") ~ "General population"),
    share_pct = if_else(scenario == "Baseline", 0L,
                        as.integer(str_extract(scenario, "[0-9]+(?=%$)"))))
}
# OFF is the 0% point of both curves
expand_baseline <- function(df) {
  off <- filter(df, mode == "OFF")
  bind_rows(filter(df, mode != "OFF"),
            mutate(off, mode = "Commuters"),
            mutate(off, mode = "General population"))
}

# Per-seed peaks, paired with the OFF run of the same seed -------------------
peak_by_seed <- policy_daily %>%
  filter(date >= policy_peak_from) %>%
  group_by(scenario, seed) %>%
  summarise(peak = max(incidence), peak_date = date[which.max(incidence)], .groups = "drop")
peak_off_by_seed <- peak_by_seed %>% filter(scenario == "Baseline") %>%
  select(seed, peak_off = peak)
stopifnot(nrow(peak_off_by_seed) == policy_expected_seeds, all(peak_off_by_seed$peak_off > 0))
peak_by_seed <- peak_by_seed %>%
  inner_join(peak_off_by_seed, by = "seed") %>%
  mutate(rel_peak = peak / peak_off) %>%
  parse_policy() %>% expand_baseline()
stopifnot(!anyNA(peak_by_seed$mode), !anyNA(peak_by_seed$share_pct))

peak_range <- peak_by_seed %>%
  group_by(mode, share_pct) %>%
  summarise(lo = min(rel_peak), hi = max(rel_peak), n = n(), .groups = "drop")
stopifnot(all(peak_range$n == policy_expected_seeds))

# Peak of the mean curve, relative to the OFF mean curve ---------------------
peak_mean <- policy_daily_mean %>%
  filter(date >= policy_peak_from) %>%
  group_by(scenario) %>%
  summarise(peak = max(incidence), peak_date = date[which.max(incidence)], .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(rel_peak = peak / peak[scenario == "Baseline"]) %>%
  parse_policy() %>% expand_baseline() %>%
  arrange(mode, share_pct)

# Targeting gain = how much more the commuter policy lowers the peak ---------
gap_by_seed <- peak_by_seed %>%
  select(seed, share_pct, mode, rel_peak) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = mode, values_from = rel_peak) %>%
  mutate(gap = `General population` - Commuters)
gap_range <- gap_by_seed %>%
  group_by(share_pct) %>%
  summarise(lo = min(gap), hi = max(gap), .groups = "drop")
gap_mean <- peak_mean %>%
  select(share_pct, mode, rel_peak) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = mode, values_from = rel_peak) %>%
  mutate(gap = `General population` - Commuters)
stopifnot(!anyNA(gap_mean$gap))

# Plots ---------------------------------------------------------------------
share_axis <- scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, 10), labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),
                                 expand = expansion(add = 2))

peak_plot <- ggplot(peak_mean, aes(share_pct, rel_peak, colour = mode)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linewidth = 0.3, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_ribbon(data = peak_range, aes(share_pct, ymin = lo, ymax = hi, fill = mode),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_point(data = peak_by_seed, size = 1, alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_line(aes(linetype = mode), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = policy_mode_colours) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = policy_mode_colours) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = policy_mode_linetypes) +
  share_axis +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_percent(), limits = c(0, NA),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), axis.title.x = element_blank()) +
  labs(y = "Peak incidence\n(% of OFF peak)", colour = NULL, fill = NULL, linetype = NULL)

gap_plot <- ggplot(gap_mean, aes(share_pct, gap)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_ribbon(data = gap_range, aes(share_pct, ymin = lo, ymax = hi),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "#D55E00", alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_point(data = gap_by_seed, size = 1, alpha = 0.4, colour = "#D55E00") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1, colour = "#D55E00") +
  geom_point(size = 2.2, colour = "#D55E00") +
  share_axis +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_number(scale = 100, suffix = " pp")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) +
  labs(x = "Share of agents quarantined",
       y = "Extra peak reduction\nfrom targeting")

brand_peak_vs_share_plot <- (peak_plot / gap_plot) +
  patchwork::plot_layout(heights = c(2, 1), guides = "collect") +
  patchwork::plot_annotation(
    title = "Brandenburg: peak incidence vs. quarantine share",
    subtitle = paste0("Peak from ", format(policy_peak_from, "%d.%m.%Y"),
                      " | Lines: mean over ", policy_expected_seeds,
                      " seeds | Ribbons/points: per-seed values vs. OFF with the same seed")) &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
brand_peak_vs_share_plot

ggsave(paste0(image_output_path, "results_brand_policies_peak_vs_share.pdf"),
       brand_peak_vs_share_plot, width = 10, height = 8)
ggsave(paste0(image_output_path, "results_brand_policies_peak_vs_share.png"),
       brand_peak_vs_share_plot, width = 10, height = 8)
write_csv(peak_mean %>% select(mode, share_pct, peak, peak_date, rel_peak),
          paste0(image_output_path, "results_brand_policies_peak_vs_share.csv"))
```

# Brandenburg Policies: relative targeting gain

Relative targeting gain = (reduction by COMMUTERS x%) / (reduction by GENERAL x%), where each reduction is 1 - outcome / OFF outcome. A gain of 1 means targeting commuters is exactly as good as quarantining the same number of random agents; 2 means it achieves twice the reduction. Outcomes are counted from `policy_peak_from` onwards (set in the peak-vs-share chunk). The ratio is unstable when the random policy barely reduces anything (small denominator), so values with a GENERAL reduction below `gain_min_reduction` are flagged and drawn as open circles. Error bars: range of per-seed gains (each seed vs. OFF with the same seed), using only seeds with a reliable denominator.

```{r brandenburg-policies-targeting-gain}
# Settings ------------------------------------------------------------------
gain_min_reduction <- 0.02  # flag ratios where random quarantine reduces < 2%
gain_metric_labels <- c(peak_incidence = "Peak incidence",
                        infections = "Infections (incl. asymptomatic)",
                        symptom_onsets = "Symptom onsets")

# Outcomes per scenario, from policy_peak_from onwards ------------------------
summarise_outcomes <- function(df) {
  df %>% summarise(peak_incidence = max(incidence),
                   infections = sum(infections),
                   symptom_onsets = sum(symptom_onsets), .groups = "drop") %>%
    pivot_longer(all_of(names(gain_metric_labels)), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value")
}
outcomes_by_seed <- policy_daily %>% filter(date >= policy_peak_from) %>%
  group_by(scenario, seed) %>% summarise_outcomes()
outcomes_mean <- policy_daily_mean %>% filter(date >= policy_peak_from) %>%
  group_by(scenario) %>% summarise_outcomes()

# Reduction relative to OFF (paired by seed where applicable) ----------------
add_reduction <- function(df, keys) {
  df %>% group_by(across(all_of(c(keys, "metric")))) %>%
    mutate(off = value[scenario == "Baseline"]) %>% ungroup() %>%
    mutate(reduction = 1 - value / off) %>%
    filter(scenario != "Baseline") %>% parse_policy()
}
reduction_by_seed <- add_reduction(outcomes_by_seed, "seed")
reduction_mean <- add_reduction(outcomes_mean, character(0))

to_gain <- function(df, keys) {
  df %>% select(all_of(c(keys, "metric", "share_pct", "mode", "reduction"))) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = mode, values_from = reduction) %>%
    rename(reduction_commuters = Commuters, reduction_general = `General population`) %>%
    mutate(gain = reduction_commuters / reduction_general,
           reliable = is.finite(gain) & reduction_general >= gain_min_reduction)
}
gain_mean <- to_gain(reduction_mean, character(0))
gain_by_seed <- to_gain(reduction_by_seed, "seed")
stopifnot(!anyNA(gain_mean$reduction_commuters), !anyNA(gain_mean$reduction_general))

gain_range <- gain_by_seed %>%
  group_by(metric, share_pct) %>%
  summarise(n_reliable = sum(reliable),
            lo = if (any(reliable)) min(gain[reliable]) else NA_real_,
            hi = if (any(reliable)) max(gain[reliable]) else NA_real_,
            .groups = "drop")

gain_table <- gain_mean %>%
  left_join(gain_range, by = c("metric", "share_pct")) %>%
  mutate(metric = factor(metric, levels = names(gain_metric_labels),
                         labels = gain_metric_labels)) %>%
  arrange(metric, share_pct)

# Table ---------------------------------------------------------------------
knitr::kable(
  gain_table %>% transmute(
    Metric = metric, Share = paste0(share_pct, "%"),
    `Reduction commuters` = percent(reduction_commuters, accuracy = 0.1),
    `Reduction general` = percent(reduction_general, accuracy = 0.1),
    `Targeting gain` = sprintf("%.2f", gain),
    `Seed range` = if_else(is.na(lo), "–", sprintf("%.2f–%.2f", lo, hi)),
    `Seeds used` = paste0(n_reliable, "/", policy_expected_seeds),
    Reliable = if_else(reliable, "yes", "no (small denominator)")),
  caption = paste0("Relative targeting gain from ", format(policy_peak_from, "%d.%m.%Y"),
                   ". Gain = commuter reduction / random reduction; 1 = no benefit of targeting."))

# Plot ----------------------------------------------------------------------
gain_plot <- ggplot(gain_table, aes(share_pct, gain)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linewidth = 0.3, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), width = 2, colour = "#D55E00", alpha = 0.6,
                na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_line(data = filter(gain_table, reliable), colour = "#D55E00", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = reliable), colour = "#D55E00", size = 2.4, fill = "white",
             na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 16, `FALSE` = 21),
                     labels = c(`TRUE` = "reliable",
                                `FALSE` = paste0("random reduction < ",
                                                 percent(gain_min_reduction))),
                     name = NULL) +
  facet_wrap(~ metric, nrow = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, 20), labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),
                     limits = c(0, 100)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom") +
  labs(title = "Brandenburg: relative targeting gain",
       subtitle = paste0("Commuter reduction / random reduction, from ",
                         format(policy_peak_from, "%d.%m.%Y"),
                         " | >1: targeting commuters beats random quarantine"),
       x = "Share of agents quarantined", y = "Relative targeting gain")
gain_plot

ggsave(paste0(image_output_path, "results_brand_policies_targeting_gain.pdf"),
       gain_plot, width = 13, height = 5)
write_csv(gain_table, paste0(image_output_path, "results_brand_policies_targeting_gain.csv"))
```

# Correlation Analysis

Both spatial levels use the mean of the same five baseline seeds, symptom-onset incidence, wave boundary, and Berlin commuter definition. Correlations are exploratory Pearson correlations; p-values are unadjusted and do not account for spatial dependence. Landkreis incidence is aggregated from the Gemeinde report using AGS county codes; locations classified as `unknown` are excluded at both levels. Peaks and peak dates are calculated from the mean incidence curves, not averaged per-seed peaks.

```{r correlation-setup}
correlation_directory <- paste0(analysis_20261006, "2-brand-comm/")
correlation_input <- paste0(analysis_shared, "misc/commuter-analysis/")
correlation_act <- "all" # Options: "work", "all"
correlation_flow <- "person" # Options: "person" (unique people), "trip" (activity starts)
correlation_sample_factor <- 4
correlation_wave_boundary <- ymd("2020-06-01")

# Choose all five baseline seeds (settings matched to ## Brandenburg above)
correlation_info <- read_delim(paste0(correlation_directory, "_info.txt"), delim = ";",
                              col_types = cols(seed = col_character())) %>%
  filter(ode == 1, commuterQuarantineMode == "OFF",
         commuterQuarantineDate == "2020-03-01", commuterQuarantineScope == "all",
         commuterQuarantineShare == 0.25)
stopifnot(nrow(correlation_info) == 5, n_distinct(correlation_info$seed) == 5)

# Require every selected baseline archive before averaging
correlation_zip <- paste0(correlation_directory, "summaries/", correlation_info$RunId, ".zip")
stopifnot(file.exists(correlation_zip))
correlation_params <- get_run_parameters(correlation_directory)

# Read all five selected ZIPs, retaining seed/configuration metadata for the helper.
correlation_raw <- map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(correlation_info)), function(i) {
  run <- correlation_info[i, ]
  member <- paste0(run$RunId, ".infections_gemeinde.txt")
  stopifnot(member %in% unzip(correlation_zip[i], list = TRUE)$Name)
  raw <- read_tsv(unz(correlation_zip[i], member),
    col_select = c(date, district, nShowingSymptomsCumulative, nSusceptible),
    col_types = cols(date = col_date(), district = col_character(),
      nShowingSymptomsCumulative = col_double(), nSusceptible = col_double())) %>%
    filter(str_detect(district, "^12[0-9]{6}$"))
  for (parameter in correlation_params) raw[[parameter]] <- run[[parameter]][[1]]
  raw
})
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(correlation_raw[c("seed", "district", "date")]))
correlation_coverage <- correlation_raw %>% count(district, date)
stopifnot(all(correlation_coverage$n == 5))

# Read shape file for gemeinden & filter to brandenburg (LK 12)
correlation_counties <- st_read(
  paste0(analysis_shared, "misc/vg5000/VG5000_KRS.shp"),
  quiet = TRUE) %>% filter(SN_L == "12") %>%
  transmute(county_ags = as.character(AGS), region = GEN)

# Shared calculation keeps the Landkreis and Gemeinde analyses identical.
regional_correlation <- function(spatial_system, shapes, berlin_id) {
  raw <- correlation_raw
  if (spatial_system == "landkreis") {
    raw <- raw %>% mutate(county_ags = substr(district, 1, 5)) %>%
      inner_join(st_drop_geometry(correlation_counties), by = "county_ags") %>%
      group_by(date, district = region, across(all_of(correlation_params))) %>%
      summarise(across(c(nShowingSymptomsCumulative, nSusceptible), sum), .groups = "drop")
  }
  raw <- raw %>% filter(district %in% shapes$region) %>% arrange(district, date)
  stopifnot(nrow(raw) > 0, !anyDuplicated(raw[c("seed", "district", "date")]),
            setequal(raw$district, shapes$region))
  daily_check <- raw %>% group_by(seed, district) %>%
    summarise(complete = all(diff(as.integer(date)) == 1L),
              positive_population = first(nSusceptible) > 0, .groups = "drop")
  stopifnot(all(daily_check$complete), all(daily_check$positive_population))
  incidence <- convert_infections_into_incidence(correlation_directory, raw, TRUE) %>%
    rename(region = district) %>% mutate(n_seeds = 5L)

  # Flow/population files are 25% sample counts; native infection reports are scaled already.
  population <- read_csv(paste0(correlation_input, "br_population__", spatial_system, ".csv"),
    col_types = cols(.default = col_character(), cnt = col_double())) %>%
    transmute(region = .data[[spatial_system]], pop = cnt * correlation_sample_factor)
  
  flows <- read_csv(paste0(correlation_input, "br_interregional-travellers-OD__act-",
    correlation_act, "__flow-", correlation_flow, "__", spatial_system, ".csv"),
    col_types = cols(from = col_character(), to = col_character(), cnt = col_double()))
  
  to_berlin <- flows %>% filter(to == berlin_id) %>% group_by(region = from) %>%
    summarise(commuters_to_berlin = sum(cnt) * correlation_sample_factor, .groups = "drop")
  
  from_berlin <- flows %>% filter(from == berlin_id) %>% group_by(region = to) %>%
    summarise(commuters_from_berlin = sum(cnt) * correlation_sample_factor, .groups = "drop")
  

  wave_metrics <- incidence %>%
    mutate(wave = if_else(date <= correlation_wave_boundary, "1", "2")) %>%
    group_by(region, wave) %>%
    summarise(max_incidence = max(incidence), max_date = date[which.max(incidence)],
              total_cases = sum(infections), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(max_day = as.numeric(max_date - min(incidence$date))) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = wave, values_from = c(max_incidence, max_date, max_day, total_cases))
  peak <- incidence %>% group_by(region) %>%
    summarise(max_incidence = max(incidence), .groups = "drop")
  merged <- shapes %>% left_join(population, by = "region") %>%
    left_join(to_berlin, by = "region") %>% left_join(from_berlin, by = "region") %>%
    mutate(across(c(commuters_to_berlin, commuters_from_berlin), ~ replace_na(.x, 0)),
           commuters_total = commuters_to_berlin + commuters_from_berlin,
           commuter_relative = commuters_total / pop,
           area_km2 = as.numeric(st_area(st_transform(geometry, 3035))) / 1e6,
           pop_density = pop / area_km2) %>%
    left_join(wave_metrics, by = "region") %>% left_join(peak, by = "region")
  stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(merged$region), all(is.finite(merged$pop)), all(merged$pop > 0))

  correlations <- expand_grid(
    predictor = c("commuter_relative", "pop_density"),
    outcome = c("max_incidence_1", "max_day_1", "total_cases_1",
                "max_incidence_2", "max_day_2", "total_cases_2")) %>%
    mutate(statistics = map2(predictor, outcome, function(x, y) {
      ok <- is.finite(merged[[x]]) & is.finite(merged[[y]])
      n <- sum(ok)
      if (n < 3 || sd(merged[[x]][ok]) == 0 || sd(merged[[y]][ok]) == 0)
        return(tibble(n = n, correlation = NA_real_, p_value = NA_real_))
      test <- cor.test(merged[[x]][ok], merged[[y]][ok], method = "pearson")
      tibble(n = n, correlation = unname(test$estimate), p_value = test$p.value)
    })) %>% unnest(statistics)

  map_titles <- c(pop = "Population", pop_density = "Population per km²",
    commuters_total = "Berlin commuters (both directions)", commuter_relative = "Berlin commuters / population",
    max_incidence = "Maximum 7-day incidence per 100,000",
    max_incidence_1 = "Peak incidence: first wave", max_incidence_2 = "Peak incidence: second wave",
    max_day_1 = "Days to peak: first wave", max_day_2 = "Days to peak: second wave",
    total_cases_1 = "Symptom onsets: first wave", total_cases_2 = "Symptom onsets: second wave")
  maps <- imap(map_titles, ~ tm_shape(merged) + tm_polygons(fill = .y) +
                 tm_title(.x) + tm_layout(frame = FALSE))
  list(incidence = incidence, merged = merged, correlations = correlations, maps = maps)
}

# Separate output folders prevent the two map sets from overwriting each other.
save_correlation_maps <- function(analysis, spatial_system) {
  directory <- file.path(analysis_shared, "figures", paste0("correlation_", spatial_system))
  dir.create(directory, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  iwalk(analysis$maps, ~ tmap_save(.x, file.path(directory, paste0(.y, ".png"))))
}
tmap_mode("plot")
```

## Correlation by Landkreis

```{r correlation-landkreis}
shp_lk <- correlation_counties %>% select(region)
brand_lk_analysis <- regional_correlation("landkreis", shp_lk, "Berlin")
brand_lk_incidence <- brand_lk_analysis$incidence %>% rename(district = region)
brand_lk_merged <- brand_lk_analysis$merged %>% rename(district = region)
brand_lk_correlations <- brand_lk_analysis$correlations
brand_lk_max_incidence_map <- brand_lk_analysis$maps$max_incidence
brand_lk_max_incidence_map
brand_lk_correlations |> view()
save_correlation_maps(brand_lk_analysis, "landkreis")
```

## Correlation by Gemeinde

```{r correlation-gemeinde}
shp_gemeinde <- st_read(paste0(analysis_shared, "misc/vg5000/VG5000_GEM.shp"), quiet = TRUE) %>%
  filter(SN_L == "12") %>% transmute(region = as.character(AGS), gemeinde_name = GEN) %>%
  group_by(region, gemeinde_name) %>% summarise(.groups = "drop")
brand_gemeinde_analysis <- regional_correlation("gemeinde", shp_gemeinde, "11000000")
brand_gemeinde_incidence <- brand_gemeinde_analysis$incidence %>% rename(gemeinde = region)
brand_gemeinde_merged <- brand_gemeinde_analysis$merged %>% rename(gemeinde = region)
brand_gemeinde_correlations <- brand_gemeinde_analysis$correlations
brand_gemeinde_max_incidence_map <- brand_gemeinde_analysis$maps$max_incidence
brand_gemeinde_max_incidence_map
brand_gemeinde_correlations |> view()
save_correlation_maps(brand_gemeinde_analysis, "gemeinde")
```
